title: The Buccaneers band under Earl Anderson
summary: He joined and then managed the Buccaneers, a small swing band, and lists its personnel.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: When I had the blue lamp I was playing music too then. I had the, I joined the Buccaneers, the band by the name of the Buccaneers. A fella by the name of Earl Anderson was the lead of the band. You know, played with them for a while and I began to get so much work. I was getting more work than he was behind me so the guy made me the manager of the band. And I still lived in for quite a while.
I don't even know that band, the Buccaneers. I don't remember that. You know, I don't know.

I remember the time we went down to play the picnic down there. I forget the name of the place. The guy saw the bills on our side, the Buccaneers. The guy came, he didn't know I was in the band. He pitched by me, man, where'd that band come from? Come from a bunch of cowboys, man. Man, we don't go any bad Buccaneers. So after we got it we played a few numbers, man. The guy was, man, those fellas can play, man. And long enough time the hall was crowded, man. Well, the fella that we had was playing piano with us by the name, his name is Bruce. He, uh, caddy out there by, by this, young, that's what, New Orleans, uh, this club out here. I know, the country club. Country club, yeah. Well, he's out there now, he don't play anymore. But he was a good entertainer. He's not much of a piano player, but he was a good entertainer. He could sing and sing on Fat Wall in style. He could, a couple of guys, name guys, he could sing on their style, you know, imitate him. And, uh...
Bruce huh? Yeah, Bruce. That's not Baby Bruce. No, no, not Baby Bruce.
Yeah, cause Baby Bruce is a mechanic of the game. Yeah. Uh, and who else was in the Buccaneers, you say? What did the leader play, you say?

Trumpet, Earl Anderson. Earl Anderson. And, uh, Charlie Temple was a guitar player. The two Knox brothers was, uh, Alto and, uh, and Tenor. That's the way we, Eddie Smith was in the band too at one time. He was a Tenor player. Well, after Eddie left, they went to Eddie Highted, uh, the other Knox boy. Edward Knox and Duncan Knox. Which plays Tenor? Uh, Duncan, uh, Edward played Tenor. Mm-hmm. Dungeons play, uh, Alto and, uh, Baritone.
Would you call that a swing band, or rhythm and blues band, or Dixieland?
Well, I said it was a swing band, a little swing band.
Did they have a trombone? No, no trombone. Bass, did you tell them? No bass. No bass. No bass.
Yeah, yeah. The drums and guitar. The drums and drums. The drums and drums and drums. Yeah. The drums and drums. Yeah. The drums and drums.
